1
Interior retaining wall calculation
Interior post and bored-pier trials for level, drained backfill. Verify site soil parameters, groundwater, foundation
movement, steel stability, sleepers, shear, ties, anchorage and end conditions. Final approval rests with the
responsible engineer.

Actions and selection
For retained height H, post spacing s, soil unit weight g and active coefficient Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi), the soil
shear is Ka g s H²/2 and the base moment is that force times H/3. Uniform surcharge adds Ka q s H and acts at H/2.
For a strip surcharge the model integrates its elastic influence over 160 wall-depth slices. Fence wind acts at H plus
half the fence height.
LC7 to LC9 use tan(phi design) = 0.85 tan(phi). The interior steel candidate is checked against LC9 bending and the
larger LC5/LC6 post-only displacement at H/200. The engineer determines the applicable combinations, restraint
and wall-end details.

Pier, embedment and cage
Founding clay strength is independent of the backfill group. A free-head rigid-pier screen and opposing concrete
bearing blocks give candidate toe and steel embedment depths, rounded up to 0.1 m with at least 0.1 m below the
embedded steel. Among the 450 to 1200 mm trials the model selects the least concrete volume meeting the
reported checks. Cage flexure uses 32 MPa concrete, N500 bars, 75 mm cover, a nominal 10 mm tie, zero axial
load and a 0.60 capacity factor.

VISUAL ENGINEERING   /   INTERIOR RETAINING WALL   /   ENGINEER REVIEW REQUIRED
2
Calculation method and units
Use metres for lengths, kPa for pressures and undrained shear strength, kN for forces, and kNm for moments in the
following wall and pier expressions.
Wall pressure and cantilever response
For a uniform surcharge q, Vq = Ka q s H and Mq = Vq H/2. Soil self-weight contributes Vg = Ka g s H²/2 and Mg =
Vg H/3. At fence height hf, the wind contributes Vw = s hf p and Mw = Vw (H + hf/2). Sum the factored terms for
each listed combination.
For a strip surcharge from setback a to b = a + width, use I(x,z) = atan(x/z) + x z/(x² + z²) at depth z. The vertical
stress increment is q [I(b,z) - I(a,z)] / pi. Multiply by Ka and the post spacing, then integrate the horizontal force and
its moment with lever arm H - z.
For post-only top displacement under soil self-weight, EI times displacement = Vg H³/15. For uniform surcharge it is
Vq H³/8, and for fence wind it is Vw (H³/3 + hf H²/4). For a strip surcharge, multiply each horizontal force increment
by x² (3H - x)/6 with x = H - z. Combine these terms at service. Post flexural resistance is 0.9 fy Ze, with consistent
units, producer effective section modulus and fy limited to 300 MPa.
Drilled depth and steel embedment
At the post base, use V and M from LC9. For diameter D and undrained founding strength su, f = V/(9 su D). Pier
peak moment Mp = M + V (1.5D + f/2). Trial toe depth L = 1.5D + f + sqrt[Mp/(2.25 su D)]. This is an ultimate
equilibrium screen for a rigid free-head pier.
Let pb equal the entered concrete bearing pressure times the flange width. The opposing uniform bearing blocks
give embedment Le = [3V + sqrt(9V² + 16 pb M)]/(2 pb). Round Le up to 0.1 m. Round the larger of L and the
adopted Le + 0.1 m up to the next 0.1 m.
Circular cage trial
For neutral-axis depth c, take a circular compression segment of depth gamma c, gamma = 0.97 - 0.0025 fc and
stress (0.85 - 0.0015 fc) fc. The trial uses fc = 32 MPa. At each bar depth y from the compression face, bar stress =
600 (1 - y/c) MPa, bounded between -500 and 500 MPa. Deduct displaced concrete in the compression block. Solve
zero axial force and sum moments about the section centre. Adopt 0.60 times the smaller nominal moment from the
two trial bar orientations. Compare it with Mp.
Spacing and cage clearance are checked before selection. At least 40 mm clearance is required from the steel
section envelope to the cage. The minimum-volume search uses pi D² L/4 at each feasible adopted diameter and
depth.
